source.title: Birational boundedness for holomorphic symplectic varieties, Zarhin’s trick for K3 surfaces, and the Tate conjecture
readSections: Entire published forty-page article: introduction and Proposition 1.5; §§2.1–2.2, §§3.1–3.4, §§4.1–4.2; every printed proof and references, pp.487–526.
Lieblich–Maulik–Snowden, arXiv:1107.1221v5 (12 March 2014), entire twenty-page manuscript including proofs and references; not the published PDF.
Charles 2013 two-page erratum, complete; it is not a Charles 2016 erratum.
Older twenty-eight-page author Charles16 PDF: only Corollary 2.7 and its discriminant argument, compared with published Corollary 2.8; not fully read.
source.versionNote: Published numbering is authoritative. The older author PDF labels the main Zarhin theorem 2.9 rather than 2.10. In LMS arXiv v5, the twisted moduli proposition is 3.4.2 (Charles cites published 3.4.1), and the partner proposition is 3.5.6 (Charles cites published 3.5.4). Published p.499 was also checked as a page image: the erroneous integer multiplier is not an OCR ambiguity.

additionalSources.read: Entire arXiv v5; publication metadata DOI 10.24033/asens.2215 checked separately.

summary: Full published-paper extraction, with the full LMS prerequisite manuscript used to restore the twisted-gerbe sign, determinant trivialization, exact geometric Brauer order and integral-lattice convention. Separates the arbitrary-field Zarhin construction, complex IHS birational boundedness and finite-field Tate arguments. Reuses pinned lattice/Hodge/Clifford/Hensel/Dirichlet APIs. Corrects the nonintegral discriminant multiplier and unpolarized finiteness conclusion with explicit counterexamples. Partial: four proof gates remain unrouted; Nikulin and other original prerequisite interiors remain proof-open. No Lean implementation or closure is claimed.

items.name: K3 surfaces
items.statement: A K3 surface over k is a smooth projective geometrically integral surface X with ω_X≃O_X and H¹(X,O_X)=0; geometric base change is denoted X_kbar. Polarizations are ample line bundles, not assumed primitive.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: base change; polarization transport; canonical bundle and H¹ access. Tests: (1) Base change of a K3 remains K3; (2) A smooth quartic surface has trivial canonical bundle; (3) An abelian surface is excluded by H¹(O)≠0.

items.name: Numerical Néron–Severi lattice
items.statement: NS(X) is the group of line bundles modulo numerical equivalence with the intersection pairing; NS(X) and NS(X_kbar) are distinguished until Galois descent is proved.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: intersection bilinearity; base change injection; divisor representative independence. Tests: (1) Numerically equivalent bundles have equal pairings; (2) H ample has H²>0; (3) Geometric NS need not equal arithmetic NS before extension.

items.name: K3 cycle-class injection and torsion freeness
items.statement: For ℓ invertible in k, c₁ embeds NS(X) into H²_et(X_kbar,Zℓ(1)); the K3 integral ℓ-adic cohomology and Picard group have the torsion-freeness used to identify numerical and cohomological divisor classes.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: ℓ-adic Mukai lattice
items.statement: For X/k K3 and ℓ≠char k, form H⁰_et(X_kbar,Zℓ)⊕H²_et(X_kbar,Zℓ(1))⊕H⁴_et(X_kbar,Zℓ(2)), with pairing (a,b,c)·(a′,b′,c′)=b·b′−ac′−a′c.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: three projections; cup pairing; Galois action; scalar extension. Tests: (1) (1,0,0)²=0; (2) (1,0,0)·(0,0,1)=−1; (3) (0,D,0)²=D².

items.name: Algebraic Mukai lattice
items.statement: N(X)=Z⊕NS(X)⊕Zω with geometric degree-one point class ω and the same pairing. It maps into every prime-to-characteristic Mukai lattice; ω is a numerical generator, not a claim of a k-rational point.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: rank/c₁/degree projections; geometric degree generator; cycle embedding. Tests: (1) (1,0,0) and ω span a hyperbolic plane with negative off-diagonal; (2) N has rank ρ+2; (3) The ω coordinate does not require a rational point.

items.name: Sheaf Mukai vector
items.statement: For a coherent sheaf F on a K3 surface, v(F)=ch(F)√td(X)=(rk F,c₁(F),χ(F)−rk F) in N(X). Tensoring by a line bundle acts by multiplication by its Chern-character exponential.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: additivity in K₀; tensor exponential; duality; RR compatibility. Tests: (1) v(O_X)=(1,0,1); (2) v(O_x)=(0,0,1) for a geometric point; (3) v(I_Z)=(1,0,1−length Z).

items.name: Mukai Riemann–Roch pairing
items.statement: For coherent F,G on X, Σ_i (−1)^i dim Ext^i(F,G)=−v(F)·v(G). This uses surface Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch, not a convention with the opposite Mukai sign.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Gieseker stability
items.statement: For a torsion-free sheaf of positive rank on a polarized smooth projective surface (X,H), compare reduced Hilbert polynomials of nonzero proper subsheaves for sufficiently large twists; strict comparison gives stability and weak comparison semistability.
items.note: The existing AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry stages supply parameter spaces, stack foundations and representability criteria, not this stable/twisted-sheaf theory. Import them into its scoped Part II. API: reduced Hilbert polynomial; subsheaf test; flat-family/base-change conditions. Tests: (1) A line bundle is stable; (2) Equal reduced polynomial is not a strict inequality; (3) Zero-rank torsion sheaves are not in this torsion-free positive-rank definition.

items.name: Stable-sheaf moduli space
items.statement: Construct M_H(v), the coarse moduli scheme of H-stable sheaves of specified Mukai vector, from bounded families and GIT/Quot; establish the relative version over the lifting DVR, with projectivity when semistability equals stability.
items.note: The existing AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry stages supply parameter spaces, stack foundations and representability criteria, not this stable/twisted-sheaf theory. Import them into its scoped Part II. API: moduli functor; coarse universal property; relative pullback; stabilizers. Tests: (1) Stable does not imply a universal sheaf on the coarse scheme; (2) An empty moduli functor must not be assigned a point; (3) Projectivity requires the semistable compactification or equality of stability notions.

items.name: Condition (C)
items.statement: For v=(r,D,s)∈N(X), require v primitive, r>0, v²>0 and gcd(r,H·D,s)=1. Neither primitivity alone nor positivity alone replaces the coprimality condition.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: primitive, rank, norm and gcd projections; transport under allowed lattice isometries. Tests: (1) (1,0,−1) satisfies (C); (2) A multiple 2v fails primitivity; (3) v=(1,0,1) fails the positive-square condition.

items.name: Coprimality excludes strictly semistable sheaves
items.statement: Under (C), χ(F(tH))=rH²t²/2+(H·D)t+s+r forces every semistable sheaf of vector v to be stable, since equal reduced Hilbert polynomials of a proper positive-rank subsheaf contradict the gcd condition.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Lifting up to ten divisor classes
items.statement: For X over algebraically closed k of characteristic p>0 and line bundles L₁,…,L_s with L₁ ample and s≤10, a finite flat DVR extension of W(k) supports a smooth projective lift of X on which all L_i lift.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Finite-height K3 lifting with Picard data
items.statement: A finite-height K3 surface over algebraically closed positive-characteristic k admits a characteristic-zero projective lift preserving the chosen Picard classes, in the finite extension of W(k) allowed by Lieblich–Maulik Cor.4.2.

items.name: Dimension argument for simultaneous lifting
items.statement: In the 19-dimensional polarized K3 deformation space the infinite-height locus has dimension 9, while imposing s−1 additional line-bundle lifts has codimension at most s−1. For s≤10 the resulting locus meets finite height; specialize its lift.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Smooth symplectic stable-sheaf moduli
items.statement: Under (C), M_H(v) is smooth projective geometrically irreducible of dimension v²+2, with one-dimensional space of global two-forms generated by an everywhere nondegenerate form.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Hilbert-scheme deformation type
items.statement: Under (C), with 2n=v²+2, M_H(v) is deformation-equivalent to X^[n] in the paper's lifting sense; over C it is an irreducible holomorphic symplectic variety. Do not strengthen this to birationality with X^[n] for every v.

items.name: Irreducible holomorphic symplectic variety
items.statement: A compact simply connected Kähler complex manifold whose H⁰(Ω²) is spanned by an everywhere nondegenerate two-form is irreducible holomorphic symplectic (IHS). Projectivity is an additional property, obtained from a positive integral (1,1)-class in the uses here.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: symplectic form up to scalar; complex deformation; projective subcase. Tests: (1) A complex K3 is IHS; (2) A product of two K3 surfaces fails h²⁰=1; (3) A symplectic torus fails simple connectivity.

items.name: Hilbert scheme of points on a K3 surface
items.statement: Construct X^[n] representing length-n zero-dimensional subschemes, its Hilbert–Chow morphism to SymⁿX, the distinct/double-point open strata and exceptional divisor.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Tests: (1) X^[1]=X; (2) X^[0] is a point; (3) X^[2] is not Sym²X along the diagonal.

items.name: Prime-to-characteristic Beauville–Bogomolov form
items.statement: For M=M_H(v), dim M=2n, each H²_et(M_kbar,Zℓ(1)) carries canonical q with (2n)!q(α)^n=n!·2^n∫α^(2n). This is the K3^[n] normalization; in dimension four ∫α⁴=3q(α)².
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Beauville–Bogomolov form on NS
items.statement: The common rational quadratic form on NS(M_kbar) is integral in characteristic zero and Z[1/p]-valued in characteristic p>0, and each prime-to-p cycle-class embedding preserves it. Equality of ℓ-adic realizations includes independence of ℓ.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: polar form; cycle compatibility; Tate twists; top-power normalization. Tests: (1) For fourfolds L⁴=3q(L)²; (2) q(mL)=m²q(L); (3) In positive characteristic no unproved Z-valued assertion replaces Z[1/p].

items.name: Mukai cohomological isometry
items.statement: For v satisfying (C) and ℓ invertible in k, the algebraic Mukai correspondence gives a canonical Galois-equivariant isometric isomorphism θ_v,ℓ:v^⊥→H²_et(M_H(v)_kbar,Zℓ(1)).
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: forward/inverse map; Galois equivariance; pairing; cycle square. Tests: (1) The target rank is v^⊥ rank; (2) The Tate twist is (1); (3) The isotropic case instead uses v^⊥/v and is not this construction.

items.name: Integral algebraic Mukai map
items.statement: For finite or algebraically closed k and (C), θ_v:v^⊥∩N(X)→NS(M_H(v)) is an injective isometry compatible with θ_v,ℓ under all cycle maps.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: injectivity; pairings; specialization; realization compatibility. Tests: (1) The map preserves q; (2) After tensor Zℓ, ℓ≠p, it matches the cohomological map; (3) A p-primary cokernel need not vanish.

items.name: Prime-primary cokernel of the algebraic Mukai map
items.statement: For the map of item 22, the cokernel is p-primary torsion in characteristic p>0 and zero in characteristic zero. The finite/algebraically closed base assumption is retained.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Quasi-universal sheaf correspondence and descent
items.statement: Use a quasi-universal sheaf with its similitude factor to define the rational cohomological and numerical Mukai maps; prove integrality using the prime-to-p realizations, lifting divisor classes, and the vanishing of Br(k) for finite/algebraically closed k.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: similitude normalization; independence; Chern-character action; base change. Tests: (1) Changing a quasi-universal multiplicity does not change the rational map; (2) A universal sheaf has multiplicity one; (3) Division by multiplicity is not itself an integrality proof.

items.name: Degeneration for a Witt-lifted sheaf moduli space
items.statement: For algebraically closed k of characteristic p and a projective W(k)-lift of (X,v,H) satisfying (C), the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of M_H(v) degenerates at E₁ if p>dim M=v²+2.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Degree-one Hodge numbers of Witt-lifted moduli
items.statement: Under item 25's W(k)-lifting hypotheses, h¹⁰(M_H(v))=h⁰¹(M_H(v))=0 for p>2.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Integral low-degree cohomology of K3 Hilbert schemes
items.statement: For a complex projective K3 surface S and n≥2, H²(S^[n],Z) is torsion-free and H³(S^[n],Z)=0; the Hilbert–Chow open-stratum calculation and codimension-two restriction prove the second assertion.

items.name: Crystalline torsion-freeness in the small-degree lifting regime
items.statement: For the W-lifted moduli spaces in Proposition 2.6, the stated Fontaine–Messing small-weight integral comparison and Hilbert-scheme topology give the H²/H³ crystalline freeness needed for the p>2/p>3 Hodge conclusions. One must verify the exact degree/prime range, not use the converse of a general torsion inequality.

items.statement: For finite or algebraically closed k, p>2, and a projective W(k)-lift (X,v,H), θ_v,η is integral and commutes with specialization. H¹(O_M)=0 and the Elsenhans–Jahnel specialization theorem supply torsion-free cokernel for NS_generic→NS_special.

items.name: Integral symmetric lattice carrier
items.statement: Use a full finitely generated Z-submodule of a rational vector space with a symmetric rational bilinear form integral on its carrier; nondegeneracy and evenness are separate predicates.
items.note: Actual declaration statement read at both recorded baseline commits as applicable. API: reuse carrier/form projections, extensionality and Gram constructors. Tests: (1) The hyperbolic plane is integral and indefinite; (2) ⟨1⟩ is integral but not even; (3) Nondegeneracy is not built into the base structure.

items.name: Half-norm discriminant quadratic form
items.statement: For an even nondegenerate integral lattice L, put A_L=L^∨/L and q_half(x+L)=B(x,x)/2 modulo Z. Charles/Nikulin use q_full=B(x,x) modulo 2Z; transport through Q/2Z→Q/Z, x↦x/2, rather than equating the two values.
items.note: Library supplies the half-norm version. The explicit full-norm/half-norm transport is a consuming conversion, not an assertion that 1/(2d)=1/(4d). API: quotient representatives; polar form; isometry transport. Tests: (1) On ⟨2d⟩ the half-norm generator is 1/(4d) mod Z; (2) Adding a lattice vector leaves the value unchanged for even L; (3) An odd L has no such half-norm descent without additional data.

items.name: Discriminant under a full sublattice
items.statement: For L⊂M integral lattices in the same rational space with the same form, disc(L)=disc(M)[M:L]², with disc the absolute determinant.
items.locator: Corollary 2.8 proof; Proposition 4.3 proof; LMS Lemma 2.1.1
items.note: Actual declaration statement read at both recorded baseline commits as applicable.

items.name: Even-overlattice isotropy criterion
items.statement: An intermediate carrier L⊂M⊂L^∨ for an even nondegenerate L is even exactly when q_half vanishes on M/L. Preserve the separate bilinear criterion for mere integrality.
items.note: Actual declaration statement read at both recorded baseline commits as applicable.

items.name: Corrected nonisotropic Mukai discriminant formula
items.statement: Let K=v^⊥∩N(X), I=[N(X):Zv⊕K], and [NS(M):θ_vK]=p^a in characteristic p>0. Then |disc NS(X)|=p^(2a)(v²/I²)|disc NS(M)|; I divides v². Thus the multiplier is a positive rational number ≤v², not necessarily an integer.
items.locator: Corollary 2.8, pp.499–500, corrected by its index proof
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Hilbert-square counterexample to integer multiplier
items.statement: For v=(1,0,−1), v²=2, M=X^[2], and odd p in the usual Hilbert-square NS comparison, disc NS(M)=2 disc NS(X). Hence disc NS(X)=p^t λ disc NS(M) cannot hold with integers t≥0, λ>0. In the lattice calculation I=2 and v²/I²=1/2.
items.locator: Corollary 2.8 literal statement, p.499; index calculation
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps.

items.name: Rank-three lattice Λ₂d
items.statement: For d>0 define Λ₂d=⟨2d⟩⊕U, with U the even unimodular hyperbolic plane. Its discriminant group is Z/(2d), with full-norm value 1/(2d) on the standard generator.
items.note: Read GN.2/GN.3 and the accepted AUDIT-02 records. Import completed integral-lattice carriers, discriminant forms and gluing; the listed embedding/arithmetic statement is not an existing declaration. API: Gram constructor; hyperbolic summand; discriminant generator. Tests: (1) rank Λ₂d=3; (2) |disc Λ₂d|=2d; (3) Full-norm and half-norm generator values differ by two.

items.name: Nikulin primitive embedding criterion in signature (2,1)
items.statement: For an even positive definite rank-two lattice Λ and n>0, existence of a primitive embedding into Λ₂n is tested by subgroups V⊂A_Λ,W⊂A₂n, an isometry γ of their restricted full-norm forms, and t>0 such that Γ_γ^⊥/Γ_γ is the cyclic form of order 2t with generator norm 1/(2t). The precise embedding-orbit classification is withheld pending the Nikulin source check.
items.note: Read GN.2/GN.3 and the accepted AUDIT-02 records. Import completed integral-lattice carriers, discriminant forms and gluing; the listed embedding/arithmetic statement is not an existing declaration. G5: no claim of a literal bijection between raw embeddings and these data.

items.name: Congruence transport of a primitive embedding
items.statement: Given d>0 and positive definite rank-two sublattice Λ⊂Λ₂d, there are N>0 and a,b≠0 such that for m>0, m≡1 mod N, gcd(m,ab)=1 and a,b squares modulo m, Λ embeds primitively into Λ₂md.
items.note: Read GN.2/GN.3 and the accepted AUDIT-02 records. Import completed integral-lattice carriers, discriminant forms and gluing; the listed embedding/arithmetic statement is not an existing declaration.

items.name: Cyclic gluing-quotient transport
items.statement: Under m≡1 mod 4dt and |A_Λ| and the finite coprimality exclusions in the proof, Id⊕m maps the old discriminant data into A_Λ⊕A₂md. The new Γ^⊥/Γ is cyclic of order 2tm; its generator has full norm 1/(2t)+y₀²(m−1)/(2md).
items.note: Read GN.2/GN.3 and the accepted AUDIT-02 records. Import completed integral-lattice carriers, discriminant forms and gluing; the listed embedding/arithmetic statement is not an existing declaration.

items.name: Generator rescaling congruence
items.statement: With the preceding gluing data, a generator of norm 1/(2tm) is obtained from λ≡1 mod 4dt and λ²ty₀²+d≡0 mod m. The assumptions that −d,t are invertible squares modulo m solve this congruence by CRT and ensure λ is prime to 2tm.
items.note: Read GN.2/GN.3 and the accepted AUDIT-02 records. Import completed integral-lattice carriers, discriminant forms and gluing; the listed embedding/arithmetic statement is not an existing declaration.

items.name: Norm-two Mukai vector and positive orthogonal class
items.statement: Choose positive definite Λ⊂Λ₂d with v²=2 and v·w=1, and nonzero l⊥v of positive norm, prime to any prescribed odd integer n when required. A transported embedding makes v primitive with gcd(rk v,Hc₁(v),s)=1; an isometry makes its rank positive.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: lattice embedding; positive-rank adjustment; v,w,l access. Tests: (1) v·w=1 implies v primitive; (2) v²=2 gives dim M=4; (3) An arbitrary positive vector need not satisfy the gcd condition.

items.name: Zarhin analogue over arbitrary fields
items.statement: For every d>0 and field k, there exist r,N>0 and a,b≠0 such that any polarized K3 (X,H)/k with H²=2md and m satisfying item 38 has v satisfying (C), c₁(v) proportional to H, dim M_H(v)=4, and a line bundle L with L⁴=r and q(L)>0.

items.name: Prime-to-n positive and ample classes

items.name: Brauer obstruction killed by a zero-cycle degree
items.statement: A geometrically defined line bundle with Galois-invariant class has a Brauer descent obstruction; if a smooth proper geometrically integral variety has a k-zero-cycle of degree e, the obstruction is killed by e, so its e-th tensor power descends.

items.name: Hilbert-square descent exponent
items.statement: For M of K3^[2]-type the top Chern number is 324=2²3⁴, yielding a degree-324 zero-cycle and descent of the 324th power of the geometric L. This explains the prime-to-6 restriction over arbitrary k.

items.name: Positive-square K3 classes can be made nef
items.statement: On a K3 surface over an algebraically closed field, a class of positive square can, after sign and reflections in effective (−2)-classes, be replaced by a big nef line bundle of the same square.

items.statement: For big nef L on a K3 surface, H¹(L)=0 and h⁰(L)=L²/2+2; the Saint-Donat fixed-part analysis reduces to a movable positive-square class or mE+Γ with E²=0, E genus one and Γ a (−2)-curve. The specified multiple becomes fixed-part-free and base-point-free.

items.statement: For a fixed K3 surface over a finite field of characteristic at least three, its k-forms constitute a finite set. This uses the automorphism action on the nef cone, finite kernel/index, and finiteness of relevant twisted conjugacy classes.

items.statement: The IHS local period map is locally an isomorphism. Keeping a positive line-bundle class of type (1,1), one can choose a small deformation with Picard rank one, where that line bundle or its dual is ample.

items.name: Kollár–Matsusaka boundedness used here
items.statement: For smooth complex projective varieties of dimension 2n with trivial canonical bundle and an ample L of fixed top self-intersection r, the polarized varieties are bounded. The general theorem controls the required intersection data; this is its K=0 specialization.

items.name: Existing polarized Hodge period-domain points

items.statement: The parallel-transport monodromy group of the fixed IHS deformation type and positive class has finite index in the subgroup of O(Λ_prim) extending to O(Λ) fixing l; choose a common finite-index torsion-free arithmetic subgroup Γ.

items.statement: For the orthogonal Hermitian symmetric domain and torsion-free arithmetic Γ in the source setting, Γ\D is a normal quasi-projective algebraic variety, with its minimal compactification.

items.name: Family period map and its algebraicity

items.statement: From the polarized primitive weight-two Hodge structure with h²⁰=1, construct the weight-one structure on its full Clifford algebra, integral lattice and polarized abelian variety, with a Clifford action and the primitive weight-zero embedding into endomorphisms of H¹.

items.statement: In the admissible setup, the h-polarized period map descends from C to K=Frac W; the closed immersion of the simultaneous (l,h) period variety into the h-period variety forces the simultaneous map and hence its l-projection to be defined over K.

items.statement: For B∈H²(X,Qℓ(1)), exp(B)(a,b,c)=(a,b+aB,c+B·b+aB²/2); it is an isometry of the rational Mukai form and exp(B)exp(C)=exp(B+C). Clearing denominators is not automatic integrality.

items.statement: For transcendental α and r=ℓ^n in the LMS exact-order scope, define the integral lattice as the Z-span of (r,α,0),(0,D,0),(0,0,1), D∈NS(X): vectors (ar,D+aα,c). Rational twisted Chow classes are exp(−B)^−1 of rational algebraic classes; the integral span is not exp(−B)^−1(N(X)).

items.statement: In LMS §3.4's scope, r=ℓ^n is the order of the Brauer class after base change to kbar. The rank of any positive-rank twisted sheaf is divisible by r; a rank-r twisted torsion-free sheaf is stable for any polarization. Merely knowing the arithmetic Brauer order is insufficient.

items.statement: For finite k of characteristic ≥5, if finitely many K3 surfaces are defined over each finite extension of k, the Tate conjecture holds for every K3 over k. The proof imports the twisted-partner construction; Charles does not invoke this criterion directly in his final argument.

items.name: Frobenius-invariant lattice discriminant bounds
items.statement: Fix rank r>0, an even weight w≥0 and q. For a nondegenerate O-lattice M, O the integers of a finite unramified extension of Qℓ, with integral characteristic polynomial for φ, all roots Weil q-integers of weight w, semisimple q^(w/2)-eigenvalue and (φx,φy)=q^w(x,y), the q^(w/2)-eigenlattice discriminant valuation is at most vℓ(disc M) for ℓ>C(r,w,q), and at most C′(r,w,q)+vℓ(disc M) for all ℓ. This controls valuations, not a common rational square class.

routes.title: K3 surfaces, Mukai moduli and holomorphic symplectic boundedness
routes.brief:
Construct the K3-specific geometry missing from the atlas and the proof architecture of Charles, Annals 184 (2016), pp.487–526. The exact geometric endpoints are Theorem 2.10: for every d>0, over any field, choose r,N>0 and nonzero a,b so that H²=2md with m≡1 mod N, gcd(m,ab)=1 and a,b squares modulo m produces a smooth four-dimensional stable-sheaf moduli space M and L with L⁴=r, q(L)>0, c₁(v) proportional to H and condition (C); include the specified prime-to-n ample class and W-lifting refinements. The complex endpoint is Theorem 3.3: fixed dimension 2n and positive top power r give uniform birational linear-series bounds after replacing L by L′ with the same top power, and hence a birationally bounded family. Do not claim uniformity for the original L, which the introduction asks as an open question.

Build numerical NS and its geometric/arithmetic distinction, the ℓ-adic/algebraic Mukai lattices, Mukai vectors and RR, lifting of at most ten divisor classes, stable-moduli smoothness, deformation to Hilbert schemes, the BB form with (2n)!q^n=n!2^n times top intersection, integral/étale θ maps and p-primary cokernel. Include the corrected discriminant formula p^(2a)(v²/I²), not an integer multiplier. Develop the IHS local/global period argument, finite monodromy index, bounded ample deformation representatives, algebraized period-covering families and codimension-two Picard transport. Supply the strong-admissibility, special-endomorphism and finite-NS arguments in p≥5, then corrected Proposition 3.17 for underlying surfaces, never infinitely varying polarized pairs.

The arithmetic branch builds the corrected LMS signed-gerbe B-field lattice, exact geometric Brauer order, isotropic moduli partners, v^⊥/Zv maps and discriminant growth. Export these geometric inputs to Algebraic cycles, pure and mixed motives (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.7) for Charles Theorems 1.3 and 1.4: Tate for all K3 over finite fields in p≥5, and for Picard rank≥2 in every characteristic including two. The latter does not use Kuga–Satake. Withhold the four quarantined items 50,113,119,127 until their named gates are discharged; their consumers remain proof-open, not unconditional formalization-ready nodes.

Import Stable and twisted sheaf moduli (AlgebraicModuliStableTwistedSheaves) for the general moduli/gerbe construction; Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II (OrthogonalIntegralModelsAndKugaSatake) for KS and good-prime models; Geometry of numbers, quadratic forms and homogeneous arithmetic (GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.2–GN.3) for the new embedding and finite-lattice theorems; existing Integral lattices (tauceti:Completed/IntegralLattices) and Hodge structures (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HodgeStructures) only through their actual pinned APIs. Import Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5), Algebraic moduli and representability (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1–R09.6), Complex comparison (ComplexComparisonPartII:C5), Crystalline cohomology (CrystallineCohomology:CR.1–CR.4), Cohomology comparisons (CohomologyComparisons:CP.2,CP.5), and the exact small-weight supplier in FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. No private duplicate cycles, crystals, moduli stacks or comparison maps. Use only the early divisor (1,1) leaf of MC.7 for Lemma 3.15, never its later K3 Tate endpoint: refine that broad stage into acyclic early/late leaves before blueprint closure. Every object needs API, three discriminating tests, and separate proof leaves for every unread cited theorem. Counterexamples 35,89,96 are regression tests, not atlas planets.

routes.title: Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry, Part II: stable and twisted sheaves
routes.brief:
Start with Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1–R09.6 and A0-extension) as first prerequisite. Its Hilbert/Quot spaces, boundedness, algebraic spaces, stackification and formal algebraization are imports, not new versions. Extend its restricted elliptic/abelian moduli scope by constructing Gieseker-stable torsion-free sheaves of positive rank on polarized smooth projective surfaces, stable and semistable parameter stacks, relative coarse schemes, and the projective moduli theorem in the precise Langer 2004 setting used by Charles Theorem 2.4. Spell out the Hilbert polynomial, boundedness, GIT quotient, flat-family descent and the difference between coarse moduli and a universal sheaf.

Build μ_r-gerbes, weight-one twisted sheaves, determinant trivializations, the signed B-field/twisted Chern character, and the period-index existence and K₀ realization input of LMS Lemma 3.4.3. In the K3 consumer, r=ℓ^n must equal the exact geometric Brauer order; rank divisibility then implies automatic stability for rank r. The fixed-determinant stack has μ_r inertia, whereas omitting the determinant isomorphism gives G_m inertia. Use the gerbe −[α_n] with LMS's exp(+α/r) vector convention and compare the untwisted B=0 case. Keep K3-specific nonemptiness, symplectic forms, dimensions, Fourier–Mukai equivalence and NS/cohomology isometries in K3SurfacesAndSymplecticBoundedness. Import intersection/Chern classes from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5, derived categories from the pinned category-theory library, and the exact Brauer/period-index supplier rather than assuming the desired rank-r sheaf. Read Langer, Lieblich and Yoshioka proof interiors before closing these nodes; currently only Charles and the full LMS manuscript have been read. Acceptance tests must distinguish stable from semistable, coarse from fine, arithmetic from geometric Brauer order, and μ_r from G_m scalar automorphisms.

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: good-prime orthogonal models and Kuga–Satake
routes.brief:
Start beyond Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties), importing its V0–V6 analytic arithmetic quotients, Baily–Borel/Borel maps and generic-fiber Hodge/abelian canonical models. Construct the full-Clifford Kuga–Satake realization of polarized weight-two Hodge structures with h²⁰=1, its spin-level orthogonal Shimura map to the polarized abelian moduli space, and the rational field-of-definition argument for the simultaneous h,l period subvariety. Import Hodge structures (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HodgeStructures), Mathlib CliffordAlgebra, AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4–A5, Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli M1–M3), and the common crystalline/étale comparison owners.

The final theorems are exactly the p≥5, prime-to-level, p-nondegenerate primitive-lattice setting of Charles equations (3.1)–(3.6) and Lemma 3.12: the family's KS map uniquely extends over W; the good-prime orthogonal model supports the finite unramified KS map needed in (3.5); the primitive twisted degree-two filtered F-crystal embeds primitively and strictly into the endomorphism crystal of H¹; and only finitely many such primitive sublattices occur over a fixed polarized level-n abelian special fiber and fixed primitive lattice. Prove independence of a characteristic-zero lift using the connection, and recover the integral image by saturation. Retain primitive and Tate-(1) labels in every fiber formula, despite their omission in printed (3.4). Use n≥3, p∤n; separate polarization parameter d₀ from degree d₀².

This is not supplied by PELModuli M4's normalizations or ShimuraCompactifications C5's good-prime PEL compactifications, whose documents explicitly reject a general integral canonical-model conclusion. Read Kisin 2010, Deligne 1972, André 1996, Rizov 2010 and the relevant Charles 2013 argument with its erratum before closing the proof. The erratum requires the degree-two/three p-torsion and even-form hypotheses in its source theorem; it is not an erratum to Charles 2016. Do not add arbitrary bad primes or all abelian-type models. The K3/IHS-specific admissibility, deformation and special-endomorphism-to-NS application belongs in the consuming K3 roadmap. Test fixed A₀ with distinct finite preimages, full versus even Clifford algebra, wrong full-H² domain, and a lattice degenerate modulo p.

The complex boundedness proof is a concrete consumer/source of the already planned Baily–Borel and Borel algebraicity theorems. No second arithmetic quotient or algebraicity theorem belongs in the K3 route.

Refine the stage before forming dependency edges: the K3 argument may consume the early leaf but cannot import its own later Tate theorem.
Surface RR, adjunction, Hodge index and intersection products are expressly in SF.5. Specialize them to K3 surfaces in the consumer without constructing a second Chow or Chern-class theory.
The complex abelian/integral-Hodge equivalence planned by A5 includes its Hom comparison. Lemma 3.15 uses this precise algebraicity of integral Hodge endomorphisms, not the general Hodge conjecture.
